turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Good morning from the Pacific side. Today is 17 November 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: We look at four themes: economy, urbanism, security and transport.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stays when the real estate tide turns?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The light on the water feels different when the numbers pull back.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The swell and the budget both speak of limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert wind carries the same quiet message across the long road south.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We listen for the essence beneath each story today.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports Los Cabos sent a 2027 revenue law of 6,746 million pesos, down 9.09 percent from the modified 2026 budget.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Own-source revenue falls nearly 20 percent to 3,338 million pesos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The city links the drop to a cooling real estate market and warns of cuts to works.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that quieter market look like on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: POSTA México adds that 2 to 3 metre surf and 30 to 50 km/h gusts hit the western coast today.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Small boats face risk from Guerrero Negro to El Pescadero.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The wind carries the same message the budget does.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The coast keeps its own rhythm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. The numbers already show the strain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does the drop in property tax and transfer tax feel when the waves keep coming?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The ocean does not pause for the revenue law.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet the city must still plan the year ahead.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 675 million pesos less will reach every project along the shore.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Pacific light still touches the same empty lots.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The real estate slowdown meets the cold front in one shared horizon.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano says residents begin collecting signatures 19 to 22 November to keep the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They want it kept as a rustic road with beach access.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2025 plan update would have abandoned 3.9 km of the 94 km San José del Cabo–La Ribera route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The road has always followed the curve of the land.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos suspended operations after high tides damaged one building and twelve rooms.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No one was hurt. Damage assessment continues.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The case brings back the question of how far buildings should sit from the shifting shore.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the line between road, beach and plan actually lie?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The signatures and the damaged rooms both point to the same edge.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Pacific light still falls on the same sand.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Grupo Questro proposed an alternative at least 1 km inland.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Implan wants a scenic drive that still touches the water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Any final choice will go to consultation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The wind moves the same palm fronds whether the plan stays or shifts.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents will stand on the beach with their pens on those four November days.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México notes Senator Susana Zatarain proposes up to ten years in prison for water theft.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos closed 25 illegal connections this year, with theft above 300 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Conagua closed two illegal sources in Cabo San Lucas that supplied about 120 tanker trucks a day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The water moves even when the law tries to hold it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS reports La Paz council approved two new buses to extend the Tiburón Urbano route to El Centenario and Chametla.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The service will link those areas with downtown using reallocated federal funds.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents have asked for better public transport for years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does the same water that is taken illegally also shape where buses can run?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Both stories circle back to daily movement.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Only three in ten people in BCS have constant supply.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The new route may ease one small part of that pressure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert road still waits for the next connection.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The wind across the dry hills carries the same scarcity each morning.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two buses and 25 closed taps meet at the same quiet crossroads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias says rain and an unfixed sewage spill are damaging the Transpeninsular highway in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The SCT office confirmed damage on the shoulders between San José and Cabo San Lucas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The spill has continued for over 20 days.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The road feels the weight of the water that should have stayed underground.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Economista reports Baja Ferries carries over 200,000 passengers a year on the Sea of Cortez routes and aims for 300 to 400,000.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They seek to turn crossings into a cruise-style experience with hotel partnerships.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 90% of goods reach the state by sea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What moves when the highway cracks and the ferry adds beds?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The sea stays the main road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The long crossings already link La Paz with Mazatlán and Topolobampo.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Packages now reach Loreto and Todos Santos as well.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The wind across the water still decides the schedule.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 20–30 partnerships with hotels already shape the voyage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Chepe train alliance extends the journey all the way to Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The ferry deck meets the desert highway under the same salt air.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: From the portal library we keep the Glasgow Declaration on Climate Action in Tourism.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It outlines decarbonization pathways for destinations.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The show Expres de Unic recently spoke with scientist Mauricio Hoyos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: His words stay with us as we look at the same coastline.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The declaration still asks what the light on the water will cost in decades ahead.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each wave carries that same quiet question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The ontology also notes the PDU gap in Mulegé.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No zoning data appears in the corpus for that northern stretch.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Tendencia 2050 sees a polycentric system rather than one repeated coastal formula.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos under water and power stress, East Cape in tension with protected areas, La Paz as service capital.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú as agricultural hub, northern Mulegé as thin corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Of 39 aquifers, 22 show deficit summing to minus 105.1 cubic hectometres a year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Vision places the water-coastal stress scenario at 42 percent likelihood.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: El Niño keeps raising tides and the second desalination plant in Cabo San Lucas reaches 75 percent completion.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Foresight lists the 2027 budget package, El Tezal partial plan and extreme tides through December.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where the measured path narrows, what still opens?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The governor places the plant at an additional 250 litres per second once finished in 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The polycentric roles already appear in the way the wind moves between each place.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: LIGIR extreme tides continue from Bahía Magdalena into La Paz Bay in December.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The sea level rise of 15 to 30 centimetres already changes the shoreline each winter.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2027 budget package of 28.3 billion pesos awaits approval.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The second plant will bring combined capacity to 655 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 5th report public event sits on 27 November at Plaza de la Reforma.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The coast writes its own limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Thank you for listening to Radio BCS2050. Come back tomorrow.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The road south still waits for the next swell.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same light will fall on the water again at dawn.
